verdicts.trueWording: indicating more syntactically complex and less reader-friendly prose
verdicts.note: arxiv.org/pdf/2510.26899 (Yasseri & Mohammadi, v5, 10 Apr 2026) fetched as PDF and converted with pdftotext. Sec. 3.2 'Descriptive Differences Between Platforms' carries the quoted words verbatim, immediately after naming Flesch-Kincaid grade (Fig. 3b) and lexical diversity (Fig. 3c) as higher on Grokipedia. Table 1 line and the Discussion repeat the same pattern.

verdicts.trueWording: only 7% of the articles had fake sources
verdicts.note: wikiedu.org blog post of January 29, 2026, byline LiAnna Davis, fetched live (HTTP 200). Body: expectation framed as 'Based on the discourse around AI hallucinations, we were expecting... citations to sources that didn't exist, but this wasn't true' before the quoted clause; the flagged set is the 178 of 3,078 articles Pangram flagged. Every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: More than two-thirds of these articles failed verification
verdicts.note: Same wikiedu.org page, paragraph directly after the fake-sources one. The page then defines the failure exactly as the claim does: a plausible-sounding sentence cited to a real, relevant-sounding source whose text does not contain the information. 'These articles' = the 178 Pangram-flagged articles.

verdicts.trueWording: GPT-4o uses present participial clauses at 5.3 times the rate
verdicts.note: arxiv.org/pdf/2410.16107 (Reinhart, Markey, Laudenbach, Pantusen, Yurko, Weinberg, Brown; v2, 21 Aug 2025) fetched as PDF. Results, 'grammatical differences' passage carries the sentence verbatim, continuing '...of humans (paired Cohen's d = 1.38)'. Author list on the PDF matches the citation; the fetched copy is the arXiv preprint of the PNAS paper, not the PNAS page itself.

verdicts.trueWording: incompatible with our policies on citation
verdicts.note: Live old.reddit.com returned a 'Welcome to Reddit' interstitial under a browser UA, and both .json routes were blocked (403 / same interstitial), so the verdict is taken from the Wayback raw capture web.archive.org/web/20260819232418id_/... . Rule 4 ('This is a DIY community'), subsection 'AI Content': generators 'tend to provide incomplete or even no proper citation for the material used to train the AI'; content from them is the quoted phrase 'and are thus not appropriate for our community'. The rule hedges with 'tend to' where the claim says flatly 'do not cite', but the stated ground of the ban is exactly the training-material citation failure.

verdicts.trueWording: generate walls of text that no one will read
verdicts.note: legendkeeper.com/worldbuilding-with-ai/ fetched live. Author's Note (Aug 12th, 2025): 'We see a lot of "Like LegendKeeper + tons of AI" competitors pop up every week now-Personally, I wonder why one would' + the quoted words. Byline Braden Herndon; the page's embedded author record gives his bio as 'Co-founder, code-lord...' and 'Braden created LegendKeeper', supporting the founder limb.

verdicts.trueWording: They don't know what they're writing.
verdicts.note: rascal.news article by Lin Codega fetched live. In Appelcline's emailed statement to Rascal: 'Despite being sold as AI, LLMs aren't intelligent.' + the quoted sentence + 'So they definitely don't understand that if you say one thing in one sentence, and then something else in another, that those two sentences create implications between them,' followed by his count of false implications in five paragraphs. The cross-sentence-implication attribution is explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: there are no links, internal or external
verdicts.note: Same rascal.news page, section opening 'what the fuck is the point of all this?': 'When you click on the profiles of any person there are no links, internal or external. No list of published work, not even a direct website...'. Two of the claim's three items are verbatim on the page; the third, 'no source references', is nowhere asserted — a grep of the whole article for citation/cited/references finds no such statement about the profiles.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: no source references — the page reports absent links and no list of published work, never absent citations

verdicts.trueWording: wasn't even mentioned in the overwrought bolus of his profile
verdicts.note: Same rascal.news page, Costikyan paragraph: 'As someone who constantly sings the praises of Greg Costikyan's Violence, imagine my surprise when that particular game' + the quoted words, then 'I suppose the AI they used wasn't clever enough to realize that Designer X was one of his pseudonyms.' Both the omission and the pseudonym attribution are Codega's own.

verdicts.trueWording: three or four paragraphs of sycophantic evasion
verdicts.note: Same rascal.news page, on her hour of questions to 4 Pillar Games through the 'Most Influential Tabletop Game Icons' Facebook page: 'every time I asked a question I was given AI-generated responses... Every single time I asked a question I got an overblown answer,' + the quoted phrase + 'with repeated phrases like "that's fair" and "public historical record"'. Every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Most end up between 1500 and 2000 words
verdicts.note: Same rascal.news page, word-count passage: she checked the word count on newly published profiles, quoted sentence verbatim, then 'I asked how long it took to write these articles, and the response was "around two hours."' Both limbs supported.

Same rascal.news page: Appelcline 'received a message from Ken Whitman on LinkedIn in January 2026' about the MITTGI profiles and wrote 'I would like to see that junk gone from the earth because you're' + the quoted phrase. Directed at Whitman, on LinkedIn, about the LLM-written designer histories.

verdicts.trueWording: It got confused and included Star Trek setting information.
verdicts.note: thealexandrian.net post fetched live; the quoted sentence is verbatim in Justin Alexander's comment, id comment-2035754, dated 'December 31st, 2025 - 3:28 pm' as the claim says, and the mission summary he quotes does import Starfleet where the game's Consortium belongs ('Starfleet (wrong) to the Consortium (correct)'). But the transcript is the Gemini share-link posted by commenter anotherpanacea at 2:33 pm; Alexander writes in the second person about it ('Then you tell it to start the playtest!'). Alexander's own hands-on test in the article body was ChatGPT, not Gemini.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: Alexander testing Gemini — the Gemini session was commenter anotherpanacea's shared transcript, which Alexander only analysed

verdicts.note: Same thealexandrian.net post, body: 'there's one thing missing from LLMs: The ability to form mental models. They can't read a text, form a mental model of what that text means...' and then 'In order to meaningfully critique something, you have to be able to form a mental model of that thing... An LLM can't do any of that. At best, it can' + the quoted words. Both limbs supported; the phrase 'Designing with ChatGPT' appears on the page as the following section, not as the heading over this passage.

verdicts.trueWording: LLMs have good spelling and bad memory
